title: Representable infinitesimal smoothness over a limit preserving fibred groupoid
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning that cartesian pullbacks exist along every base morphism and each fibre is a groupoid. A local ring has a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. Assume $\mathcal X$ preserves small directed affine limits: for every such inverse system $(T_i)$ with limit $T$, the natural functor $2\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal X(T_i)\to\mathcal X(T)$ is an equivalence. Let $U$ be a scheme of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $x\in\mathcal X(U)$. Write $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$ as a discrete groupoid, with the morphism $h_U\to\mathcal X$ given by pullback of $x$. Assume this morphism is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal X(T)$, its $2$-fibre product with $h_T$ is an algebraic space. Assume the following lifting property: For each field $l$ of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}l\to U$, each surjection $B'\to B$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras whose residue fields are identified with $l$, each $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$ restricting to $\alpha$, each $z\in\mathcal X(B')$, and each isomorphism $z|_B\cong a^*x$, there exist a lift $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to U$ of $a$ and an isomorphism $z\cong(a')^*x$ extending that isomorphism. Then $h_U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth: for every such $T$ and $y$, the projection $U\times_{\mathcal X}T\to T$ is a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces, meaning that its composites with etale scheme charts are smooth morphisms of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. No stack-descent, Rim-Schlessinger, effectivity or tangent-dimension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07XX (lemma-implies-smooth), specialized to h_U with U finite type over a Noetherian affine base; Tag 07XN (lemma-limit-preserving-algebraic-space) supplies limit preservation of h_U because U is locally of finite presentation.

proof.text: The one affine chart $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally Noetherian by the definition. Since $U\to S$ is of finite type, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes it locally of finite presentation. Thus [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test], applied to the scheme $U$ as an algebraic space, says that $h_U$ preserves directed affine limits. Fix an affine $V\to S$ locally of finite presentation and $y\in\mathcal X(V)$. The same limit-test lemma makes $h_V$ limit preserving. Let $Z=h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_V$, an algebraic space by the assumed representability.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, first paragraph; Tag 07XN for h_U and h_V

proof.text: We check limit preservation of $Z$ directly. An object over $T=\lim_iT_i$ is $(u:T\to U,v:T\to V,\theta:v^*y\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*x)$. Descend $u,v$ to a common stage using step 1. Full faithfulness of $2\operatorname{colim}\mathcal X(T_i)\to\mathcal X(T)$ descends $\theta$ after increasing the index. Hence the object descends. For two stage triples, an arrow is precisely equality of the two $U$ maps and of the two $V$ maps, with equality of their displayed isomorphisms in $\mathcal X$. The first two equalities hold at a common later stage by step 1; the third holds later by faithfulness of the same colimit functor. Such an arrow is unique, since both representable groupoids are discrete. This proves full faithfulness as well as essential surjectivity. An algebraic space viewed as a fibred groupoid is an algebraic stack: its sheaf property gives object descent, its diagonal is representable, and its etale scheme atlas is a smooth atlas. Applying [lem-sfb-stack-limit-preserving-lfp] to $Z$ gives local finite presentation of $Z\to S$.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, first paragraph, using Tag 07XM; the omitted fully-faithful bookkeeping is written here

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $p:W\to Z$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The chart $p$ is etale, hence locally of finite presentation, and $Z\to S$ is locally of finite presentation by step 2; the composition law of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] for morphisms representable by algebraic spaces gives local finite presentation of $W\to S$ and hence local finite type (the finite generators in a finite presentation generate the algebra). The projection $q:W\to V$ is locally of finite type by [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation], applied to $W\to V\to S$. Also $V$ is locally Noetherian: it is locally of finite type over the locally Noetherian $S$, as stated in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. We will apply the criterion [lem-sfb-scheme-artinian-smoothness-finite-type-tests] to $q$.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, choice of W and the hypotheses of the scheme lifting criterion

proof.text: Take a test square for that criterion: a small extension $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$, $b:\operatorname{Spec}B\to W$, and a finite type map $c:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V$ with $qb=ci$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V\to S$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), since local finite presentation supplies finite algebra generators. Any open neighborhood of the closed point of a local spectrum is the whole spectrum: a principal neighborhood $D(g)$ has $g$ outside the maximal ideal, hence a unit. Applying the affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] to this composite therefore makes $B'$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Its quotient residue field $l$ is generated by the images of these generators, so $l$ is of finite type over $R$. The triple $pb$ is $(a,c|_B,\theta:(c|_B)^*y\cong a^*x)$. Apply the assumed lifting property at the $l$-point of $U$ induced by $a$, with $z=c^*y$ and $\theta$. It gives $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to U$ and $\theta':c^*y\cong(a')^*x$, restricting to $a,\theta$. Thus $(a',c,\theta')$ is a map $d:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to Z$ with $di=pb$ and projection $c$. The supplied isomorphism, including its restriction, has been retained.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, base change of the deformation lifting condition; explicit triple construction

proof.text: The small extension has square-zero kernel, so $i$ is a first order thickening of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-space-infinitesimal-lifting] to the etale map $p:W\to Z$, the map $d$, and $b$. It gives $b':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to W$ with $b'i=b$ and $pb'=d$. Projecting to $V$ yields $qb'=c$. Thus every test square from step 4 lifts.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, lifting through the etale chart (the use of Tag 07XV)

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-scheme-artinian-smoothness-finite-type-tests], $q:W\to V$ is smooth. The property smooth for scheme maps is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] to the presentation $W\to V$ of $Z\to V$, whose source chart $p$ is surjective and whose target chart is the identity of $V$. It follows that $Z\to V$ is smooth on every etale presentation.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, conclusion on W and then Z; Tag 02HY packages the finite-type-point argument

proof.text: For maps of algebraic spaces to schemes, smoothness is stable under arbitrary scheme base change by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to algebraic spaces as algebraic stacks. It is Zariski local on the scheme target: given a target open cover $T=\bigcup_jT_j$, put $Z_j=Z\times_TT_j$. If each $Z_j\to T_j$ is smooth, compose with the open immersion $T_j\to T$, etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and hence smooth by the cited calculus. Its composition law gives smoothness of each $Z_j\to T$; its open-source-cover law gives smoothness of $Z\to T$. The converse is base change. Thus smoothness satisfies both property hypotheses of [lem-sfb-limit-test-representable-property]. Apply that lemma to $h_U\to\mathcal X$. The target is limit preserving on objects by the assumed equivalence of groupoids, representability is assumed, and step 6 supplies every affine locally finitely presented test. Consequently $h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_T\to T$ is smooth for every $T,y$, as required.

source.place: Tag 07XX proof, reduction using Tag 07WI and conclusion for arbitrary T

proof_origin.place: Tag 07XX (lemma-implies-smooth), proof, specialized to h_U; the final scheme step uses Tag 02HY (lemma-lifting-along-artinian), whose proof supplies the finite-type-point argument of Tag 07XX.

tool_uses.why: Generic Noetherian-base conversion of local finite type to local finite presentation, used in step 1; the unit has no replacement for this ring-theoretic finiteness law.
Only clause (e), composition of locally finite type scheme maps, is used in step 4 to verify the residue field hypothesis. This is a generic scheme law, not a different proof route.
Only the generic scheme fact that target-open inclusions are etale is used in step 7 to verify Zariski locality of smoothness in the property test.
